questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Relevant courses, big international community at the university and an active student culture with events.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a local student who helped us with introducing us to the university and city. He showed us where to find relevant information and showed us around.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There was not housing on campus, but instead the university had recommended a housing foundation that has multiple dormitories close to campus. It was linked directly to on the university website.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: All the dormitories are owned by the same housing company and everything is quite stream-lined. If something is missing or doesn't work in the apartment, make sure to write an email to the housing foundation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived with 11 other people in a dorm with only two bathrooms and two very small kitchens, so sometimes it felt a bit cramped and you had to wait in line to cook.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When we arrived for the orientation for the international students, the course registration had already passed and some of my courses had even already started, which we had not been informed about. Luckily it was still quite easy to sign up, as I just wrote to the study coordinator and she signed me up for the courses where the registration period had passed.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can sign up in two ways. By the Tuudo app or through their only system Peppi. I used the tuudo app, as it was quite simple.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The study coordinator was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's simple, but if the registration period has passed, then write to your study coordinator at the host university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some courses were good and some were not.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of the courses were easier than I expected, but the content was still fulfilling. One course was not very good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were much fewer lectures and exercise classes and more self-studying.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Survival finnish
Beginner's finnish level 1
Advanced Quantum Mechanics
Quantum devices
Nummerical Programming
Plasma physics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Advanced quantum mechanics and quantum devices were good courses. If you want to learn finnish, then take the beginner's finnish level 1, but the survival finnish covers very basic things which you can learn on your own through e.g. Duolingo.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Their campus is not open 24/7 unless you buy a card for 20€ that let's you have free access to the campus at all times.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Daily items like milk products where way cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of student societies, for basically everything, if you looked for it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
UniMove: offers lessons in different sports to the students for a cheap semester price.
Be active in the guild associated to your studies or find a guild for a sport or creative endeavor.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking or skating. Go to a sauna - I can recommend the floating sauna in the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a guild or society on campus. They might seem shy and hesitant to speak finnish, but they are quite friendly. They are especially talkative in a sauna at a party after getting a few drinks.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't remember if there were any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The sauna culture was great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You have a lot of free time in your studies so use it to explore and experience things.
Try to meet local people and not just other exchange students: Your guild is a good starting point or joining a non-academic guild.
Participate in everything! Join the parties and events and speak with people!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I have made, both with other exchange students but also with local people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
All the bureacratic things that you have to sign and send and so on. It's a needed part, but it could sometimes be a little stressful.
Otherwise leaving after completing the exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
